html:
Prithviraj Chauhan was the Rajput king of the Chahamana dynasty who ruled from Ajmer and Delhi from about 1178 to 1192, and lost north India's decisive battle to the Ghurids.

He became king as a boy and fought his Rajput neighbours, the Chandelas and the Chaulukyas of Gujarat. In 1191 he beat Muhammad of Ghor at the first battle of Tarain. The next year Muhammad came back with a better army and won the second battle of Tarain. Prithviraj was captured and soon killed.

His defeat opened the Ganges plain to the Ghurids, whose general founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

Later poets made him a hero. The Prithviraj Raso, a Hindi epic finished centuries after him, tells of his elopement with Samyukta, daughter of his rival Jayachandra of Kannauj, and of a blinded Prithviraj killing Muhammad with an arrow. Most of this is legend. He remains a symbol of Rajput courage.
sum: Prithviraj Chauhan was the Rajput king of the Chahamana dynasty who ruled from Ajmer and Delhi from about 1178 to 1192, and lost north India's decisive battle to the Ghurids.
